unresolved.finding: When UPPER_CASE_MOD is enabled, the generated TYPESIZES.mod and NETCDF.mod files are declared as installed headers but CLEANFILES removes only lowercase typesizes.mod and netcdf.mod, so uppercase module artifacts may remain after cleanup.

The uppercase-module configuration installs and builds TYPESIZES.mod/NETCDF.mod, but CLEANFILES is fixed to lowercase typesizes.mod/netcdf.mod, leaving uppercase module files outside clean cleanup on case-sensitive systems.

The option is documented as --with-netcdf=DIR, but any slash-containing value (including a directory such as /opt/netcdf) is assigned directly to LIBS_NETCDF and passed as a linker argument rather than being translated into include/library search flags.

The Fortran preprocessor fallback is hard-coded to /lib/cpp -C -ansi without checking that the executable exists or selecting a configured system preprocessor, so configurations lacking that exact path can fail or use an unsuitable preprocessor.
The preprocessing failure message says 'Fortran does do preprocessing', which is grammatically incorrect and obscures the intended configure failure reason.
AX_FC_HAS_MODULE uses the single cache key ax_cv_fc_has_module for every module argument, so the result of the first module probe can be incorrectly reused for later different modules.
The macro defines HAVE_$1 via AC_DEFINE but tests the shell variable HAVE_$1 in AM_CONDITIONAL without assigning it, so the generated conditional can remain false even when the module probe succeeds.

The package metadata enables tag_svn_revision, a legacy Subversion-oriented egg_info setting, despite the repository's build scaffolding otherwise being autotools/Visual Studio based; its active consumer and intended release behavior are unclear.

The USENETCDF branch uses NETCDF_CFLAGS for Fortran compilation and separately appends -lnetcdff to global LIBS, while the nearby comment explicitly questions NETCDF_FCFLAGS/FFLAGS; Fortran include/link flags and library ownership are therefore an unclear configure contract.

The dependency rule regenerates $(deps) from $(xbeach_SOURCES) but the included dependency file is not listed as a generated/clean target, so stale or missing dependency metadata can affect incremental builds without an explicit lifecycle.

The distribution script performs destructive recursive removal and multiple wildcard copies without checking command success, so a missing input, failed mkdir, or copy error can still yield an apparently completed but incomplete distribution.
The zip script does not check whether copying 7za.exe, changing directory, archive creation, or deletion succeeded, so it can silently leave a missing or incomplete archive.

The MPI_netcdf configurations contain no PreprocessorDefinitions for USEMPI or USENETCDF, unlike the separate MPI and netcdf configurations, so their names do not match the feature flags they appear intended to enable.
The netcdf_Release|x64 configuration writes object files to bin\win32\$(ConfigurationName) while its output/module paths are bin\x64, mixing architectures/configuration directories.
MPI_Release|x64 searches ..\xbeachlibrary\bin\static\$(ConfigurationName) for the second include directory instead of the x64 path used by the same configuration's first directory.
MPI_netcdf_Debug|x64 uses bin\win32\$(ConfigurationName) for both ModulePath and ObjectFile despite being an x64 configuration, causing cross-configuration artifacts.

version.dat is generated from live svnversion, svn info, and date commands with no fallback or command-failure handling, so builds outside an SVN checkout can produce empty metadata or fail depending on shell/error policy.
The rmdir command leaves the %2\mpich path unquoted even though the same script accepts a SolutionDir/TargetDir path that may contain spaces.

For a 32-bit build on a 64-bit machine, if the x86 MPICH2 installation is absent the fallback copies C:\Program Files\MPICH2, which is likely the 64-bit installation, into the Win32 target without validating its architecture.
The DLL copy operations are unconditional and their failure status is not checked, so missing platform/configuration NetCDF inputs can leave an incomplete target without an explicit failure.

The script constructs the working directory as %SolutionDir%scripts without inserting a separator and invokes dist\generate.exe without checking either cd or executable success, making correctness depend on an undocumented trailing separator and silent failure possible.

When RevisionNumber is defined the script writes version.dat in the current directory, whereas the normal and fallback paths target includes\version\version.dat, so the same script can produce metadata in different locations.
Automatic version generation depends exclusively on the hard-coded TortoiseSVN executable path C:\Program Files\TortoiseSVN\bin\SubWCRev.exe, with no configurable override or alternate VCS path.

Both netcdf_Release configurations invoke/copy NetCDF artifacts from the Debug directory (..\..\lib\win32\netcdf\Debug and ..\..\lib\x64\netcdf\Debug), so release builds can link or distribute debug libraries.
The netcdf_Release configurations use the Debug NetCDF library directory for both Win32 and x64, so release builds can link against debug libraries.
Both MPI_netcdf x64 configurations use the Debug NetCDF library directory, including MPI_netcdf_Release|x64, creating a release/debug dependency mismatch.
